entrypoints.summary: POST /register accepts form field name, signs that value into the jwt_auth cookie, and uses the name in a concatenated SQLite SELECT.
GET /api decodes jwt_auth, takes its name claim, concatenates it into the notes owner predicate, executes it, and renders returned descriptions.

affected_components.role: Accepts attacker-controlled name and places it in the signed jwt_auth identity claim.
Decodes the claim, constructs the owner-filter SQL text, executes it, and renders returned note descriptions.
Seeds admin-owned notes, including a flag-bearing description.

impact.affected_asset: Rows in the SQLite notes table belonging to other owners; specifically the seeded admin note containing challenge flag material.
impact.attacker_capability: Manipulate the SQL predicate used to retrieve notes by registering a SQL-syntactic name that is subsequently carried in a valid application-signed JWT claim.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized disclosure of note descriptions, including the seeded admin-owned flag-bearing note in this challenge dataset.

causal_trace.summary: An HTTP client controls the name form field submitted to POST /register; only the exact value admin is rejected.
The application signs the attacker-provided name into jwt_auth, then GET /api treats the decoded name claim as SQL query text rather than exclusively as an owner data value.
GET /api builds SELECT description FROM notes WHERE owner == '<name>'; by string concatenation and passes the resulting string to sqlite3 cursor execute.

A SQL expression carried through the name claim can alter the notes-selection predicate, exposing descriptions outside the claim's intended owner scope; initialization includes an admin-owned note containing flag material.

failure.operation: SQLite cursor.execute on a dynamically concatenated owner predicate in GET /api

primary_invariant.statement: The owner value used to select notes must be bound as data, so a decoded identity claim selects only rows whose owner equals that identity.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The decoded jwt_auth name claim is concatenated inside a SQL string and consequently can be interpreted by SQLite as predicate syntax.

quality.review_notes: The supplied application source directly establishes the source-to-sink path and seeded sensitive note. No exploit request/response, execution result, solve script, or delivered remediation patch is included. The dataset flag is explicitly fake, so it evidences challenge oracle material rather than disclosure from a live deployment. Provenance is a public archive mirror rather than demonstrated organizer-origin source.

remediation.invariant_restored: Bind the decoded name claim as the owner parameter for the notes query rather than interpolating it into SQL text, ensuring it remains a value and cannot alter the predicate.
mitigation_classes: parameterized SQL query for owner lookup

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Submit a non-admin name containing SQL-relevant characters such that it can be encoded in the issued jwt_auth cookie and later reach the GET /api query construction.
data_structure_invariants: The JWT name claim is intended to identify an owner value.
The notes.owner comparison is intended to restrict returned rows to the authenticated owner.
The code does not preserve the claim as a bound value when constructing the GET /api SQL query.
state_context.state_machine: A client submits a name during registration, receives a jwt_auth cookie containing that name, then presents that cookie to GET /api, where the decoded claim becomes part of the notes lookup.

target.component: Flask registration and notes API backed by SQLite
